items.question: Who can participate in the conference?
answer: The conference welcomes scholars, educators, practitioners, students, researchers, community partners, and others working on issues related to sustainable cities and landscapes.
Participants do **not** need to be affiliated with an APRU member university in order to submit an abstract or attend the conference.

items.question: Is virtual participation available?
answer: No. **APRU-SCL 2027 will be held fully in person in Singapore.** Virtual oral presentations, digital poster presentations, and online participation will not be available.

items.question: I am unsure which track my abstract belongs to. What should I do?
answer: Please select the track that you feel most closely aligns with your research. The track categories are intentionally broad.
During the review process, the Organising Committee may also invite reviewers from another track to assess an abstract if their expertise is considered more appropriate to the submission.

items.question: Can I submit research that does not fit exactly within one of the ten tracks?
answer: Yes. The listed tracks are intended to provide broad thematic guidance and are not necessarily exhaustive. Authors should select the track that most closely relates to their submission.

items.question: Can researchers from universities outside the APRU network submit?
answer: Yes. Submissions are welcome from researchers and practitioners regardless of whether their institution is an APRU member.

items.question: Are accepted abstracts automatically included in a Working Group?
answer: No. **The Call for Abstracts and Working Group participation are separate.**

Acceptance of an abstract for an oral or poster presentation does not automatically provide access to a Working Group. Participants interested in joining a Working Group may indicate their interest during conference registration.

items.question: Are there awards for presentations?
answer: Yes. Accepted paper and poster presentations will be eligible for consideration for the **Best Paper Award** and **Best Poster Award**, respectively.

items.question: Is full paper submission compulsory after my abstract is accepted?
answer: No. Submission of a full paper is optional. However, once an abstract has been accepted, **presenters are required to submit the relevant presentation file for an oral presentation or poster file for a poster presentation.**
Please note that **only submissions accompanied by a full paper will be considered for the Best Paper Award.**

items.question: How do I join a Working Group?
answer: You will be able to **register your interest in a Working Group during conference registration**, which opens on **15 January 2027**.
Participants who express interest in a specific Working Group will be contacted by the respective Working Group leaders regarding participation and any preparation required before the conference.

items.question: Can I present an abstract and participate in a Working Group?
answer: Yes. Oral and poster presentations and Working Group participation are separate components of the conference.
Where a presenter is also participating in a Working Group, the conference organisers will seek to coordinate the schedule so that the participant can attend both activities.

items.question: Does joining a Working Group require an abstract submission?
answer: No. The open Call for Abstracts and Working Group participation are separate processes.

items.question: Do presenters need to register for the conference?
answer: Yes. **Registration is required for all participants**, including presenters with accepted oral or poster presentations and participants in Working Group sessions.

items.question: What are the registration fees?
answer: The conference offers three registration categories:
Early registration closes on **28 February 2027**, and standard registration closes on **20 April 2027**.

items.question: Who is eligible for the Southeast Asia registration rate?
answer: The SEA rate applies to participants from **Southeast Asian countries**.

items.question: Is there a special registration rate for NUS students or faculty?
answer: NUS students and faculty are required to pay the applicable conference registration fee.
NUS students may wish to check with their department, programme administrator, supervisor, or relevant funding office regarding any funding or reimbursement available for conference participation.

items.question: Does APRU-SCL 2027 provide travel grants, accommodation support, scholarships, or financial assistance?
answer: No. **APRU-SCL 2027 and the NUS Department of Architecture do not provide travel grants, accommodation funding, or other financial assistance for conference participation.**

Participants, particularly students and early-career researchers, are encouraged to check with their home institution, department, programme administrator, supervisor, research grant, or other relevant funding body to determine whether conference travel or registration support may be available.

items.question: Are travel and accommodation included in the registration fee?
answer: No. Participants are responsible for arranging and covering their own travel and accommodation.

items.question: Will there be field trips during APRU-SCL 2027?
answer: Yes. The conference will offer **half-day field trips** exploring Singapore’s approaches to sustainable urbanism.
The field trips cover five broad themes:
Activities may include guided walks, cycling tours, and site visits.

items.question: How do I select a field trip?
answer: Participants will select their preferred field trip during conference registration.
Some field trip options may require an **additional fee**.

items.question: How do I join the Student Network Session?
answer: Participants will be able to indicate their interest in the Student Network Session during conference registration.
Further session details will be announced in **March 2027**.

items.question: Do I need a visa to attend the conference in Singapore?
answer: Visa requirements depend on your nationality and travel circumstances. Participants should consult the [Singapore Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)](https://www.ica.gov.sg/) for the latest entry and visa requirements applicable to them.

items.question: Can the conference provide an invitation letter for my visa application?
answer: Invitation letters for visa application purposes will only be provided **after the registration fee has been paid or a registration fee waiver has been granted upon request**.
The NUS Department of Architecture will not submit visa applications on behalf of participants.
